qa_l1_consulted: qa-l1.json verdict=PASS (8/8 conformance checks). QA-L1 verifies wiring/shape; the findings below are correctness/security gaps QA-L1 does not exercise (no real DB, no real downstream services).
verdict_rationale: Two HIGH findings (saga_log empty-UUID aborts the wrapping tx so idempotency_keys never finalizes — every successful commit silently rolls back; and inventory.reservation.create / inventory.reservation.release / payment.intent.create are sent with customer-JWT only, missing X-Internal-Secret — recipients enforce InternalAuth so every commit will 401 at step 6 in real integration). Hot-zone deltas (Idempotency-Key per-customer scope, INFLIGHT race, server-side pricing strict, §11.2 single source, buyerEmail wire) are otherwise implemented correctly.

findings.topic: saga_log INSERT receives empty string for UUID NOT NULL column — aborts the wrapping checkout tx, so the idempotency_keys finalize never persists; client gets the response but the row stays INFLIGHT, and after 60s the janitor flips to ABANDONED, opening a re-execution path that produces a SECOND order/reservation/payment-intent for the same Idempotency-Key.
findings.locus: backend/services/checkout/app/checkout/handler_commit.go:193-203 (finalizeAndReturn closure) and handler_commit.go:197 (sagaLogStore.Write call); migration backend/services/checkout/migrations/002_create_saga_log.up.sql:6 (order_id UUID NOT NULL)
findings.description: The finalizeAndReturn closure is the single saga writer. It hard-codes the orderID argument as the empty string (`s.sagaLogStore.Write(c.Request.Context(), tx, "", customerUserID, traceID, sagaStatus, steps, compensation)`) and is invoked on every terminal path — including the success path at handler_commit.go:513 where a real orderIDStr is in scope but never threaded into the closure. The migration declares `order_id UUID NOT NULL`. Postgres rejects an empty string cast to UUID with `invalid input syntax for type uuid: ""`, putting the surrounding pgx tx into an aborted state. The next statement (tx.Commit) returns `current transaction is aborted, commands ignored until end of transaction block` and Postgres rolls back the whole tx. The error from sagaLogStore.Write is intentionally discarded with `_ =` and the tx.Commit error is only logged at slog.Error level — c.Data still writes the success envelope to the wire, so the client sees HTTP 201 / orderId / paymentIntent. But the idempotency_keys UPDATE that flipped the row to COMPLETED is rolled back too. Subsequent retries with the same Idempotency-Key see status=INFLIGHT (returns 409 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_INFLIGHT for ~60s), then status=ABANDONED after the janitor sweep; the ABANDONED branch (handler_commit.go:162-183) then DELETEs the row and re-INSERTs INFLIGHT, runs the full orchestration again, and produces a second reservation + a second order + a second payment-intent (all of which will succeed because they are idempotent on the SAME orderId — except orderId is regenerated at handler_commit.go:336 every entry, so the recipient idempotency caches do NOT match and a duplicate set of side-effects DOES land). The QA-L1 OBS-04 entry flags the empty-orderID write but only as low-severity 'forensics gap' — it does not trace through the tx-abort consequence. Unit tests miss this because handler_commit_test.go uses a zero-value Service and never exercises the DB tx path.
findings.recommendation: Three remediations, any one suffices: (a) skip sagaLogStore.Write when orderID is empty — pre-step-5 errors do not need a saga row since no remote state was mutated; (b) make migration column `order_id UUID NULL` and pass nil from Go on early-fail paths (saga_log is operational-only, not an FK target); (c) change finalizeAndReturn to accept orderID as a closure-captured variable and thread the real orderIDStr through after step 5 (and `""` → use a sentinel UUID like uuid.Nil pre-step-5, with a CHECK constraint adjustment). Recommend (a) — minimal change, preserves the 'saga_log is for orchestration paths' invariant. CRITICAL: any fix must also stop swallowing the sagaLogStore.Write error; either rollback the tx on saga_log failure (consistent with current behavior, but the client-visible response should then surface the failure) OR run sagaLogStore.Write in a separate tx after the main commit so the request does not depend on it. Add an integration test that asserts idempotency_keys.status=COMPLETED after a successful commit AND that a second call with the same key returns the cached envelope.
owasp_refs: OWASP API3:2023 Broken Object Property Level Authorization (idempotency contract)

findings.topic: inventory.reservation.create / inventory.reservation.release / payment.intent.create are called with customer-JWT only — X-Internal-Secret header is never set. Per ADR-008 + connectivity.md these hops are X-Internal-Secret-authenticated; recipients enforce InternalAuthMiddleware (verified in inventory/router/router.go:87 and payment/router/router.go:61-66). Every commit will receive 401 at step 6 → step 7 compensation fires unnecessarily; in addition, the customer's bearer JWT is leaked to internal services that should not see it.
findings.locus: backend/services/checkout/app/checkout/client_inventory.go:58 (BulkReadStock), :120 (CreateReservation), :179 (ReleaseReservation); backend/services/checkout/app/checkout/client_payment.go:56 (CreateIntent); backend/services/checkout/router/deps.go:46-52 (Inventory + Payment clients constructed without internalSecret); backend/services/checkout/app/checkout/client_inventory.go:21-29 (no internalSecret field); backend/services/checkout/app/checkout/client_payment.go:19-25 (no internalSecret field)
findings.description: client_order.go correctly threads cfg.InternalAuth.SharedSecret into NewOrderClient and sets internalSecretOption on every call. client_inventory.go and client_payment.go do not. Concrete consequences: (1) integration: inventory's reservation router applies inventory.InternalAuthMiddleware which constant-time-compares X-Internal-Secret; checkout sends no such header → 401 AUTH_INVALID. (2) integration: payment.intent.create has internalSecretMW that rejects on missing header → 401. (3) security: customer's Authorization Bearer JWT is forwarded to inventory and payment via bearerAuthOption — these services should authenticate the CALLING SERVICE (checkout), not the originating customer. Forwarding the JWT both expands the trust boundary (inventory/payment can now act-as the customer toward identity / cart) and is contrary to td.json §security_notes ('the customer JWT is forwarded only to identity.profile.read, identity.address.list, cart.read, and cart.clear-on-checkout — the four customer-context hops; steps 6/7/8 + compensations use X-Internal-Secret only'). Note: inventory.stock.bulk-read is the one exception — its actual implementation requires customer JWT (inventory/router/router.go:65-72 puts /stock under JWT middleware), which contradicts the spec but matches the current code; that drift belongs to Reviewer-L2. The reservation.create / reservation.release / payment.intent.create gaps are unambiguous and within checkout's ownership.
findings.recommendation: Add an `internalSecret string` field to InventoryClient and PaymentClient; thread cfg.InternalAuth.SharedSecret in deps.go; add `internalSecretOption(c.internalSecret)` to the option-list of CreateReservation, ReleaseReservation, CreateIntent. Drop bearerAuthOption from the same three calls (the spec says X-Internal-Secret only on these hops; keeping the bearer doubles the trust surface for no benefit). Keep bearerAuthOption on BulkReadStock until inventory's stock-side route is reconciled — that reconciliation is REV-L2 territory. Add a unit test for each client that asserts the outgoing request contains `X-Internal-Secret` with the configured value AND does NOT contain `Authorization: Bearer` for reservation.create / reservation.release / payment.intent.create.

findings.topic: Idempotency-Key HTTP header is never set on outbound calls to inventory.reservation.create, order.create-from-checkout, order.cancel-on-checkout-failure, or payment.intent.create — all four contracts (connectivity.md:81-83 + design/spec/order-order/create-from-checkout.md:78 + design/spec/order-order/cancel-on-checkout-failure.md:46 + design/spec/inventory-reservation/create.md:24) declare it as a required header equal to orderId. Code only places idempotencyKey inside the JSON body.
findings.locus: backend/services/checkout/app/checkout/client_inventory.go:108-148 (CreateReservation builds reservationCreateRequest.IdempotencyKey but no header set on PostWithOptions); client_order.go:74-110 (CreateFromCheckout puts orderId inside the body but does not add an Idempotency-Key header); client_order.go:120-164 (CancelOnCheckoutFailure has no idempotency header at all); client_payment.go:43-81 (CreateIntent has no idempotency header at all)
findings.description: Per cross-cutting.idempotency.internal_orderId_rule and the per-spec entries above, internal callers MUST send the orderId as the `Idempotency-Key` HTTP header. Order's actual handler currently reads the value from the JSON body (handler_create_from_checkout.go:80 reads req.IdempotencyKey), so the runtime impact today is benign for create-from-checkout. But the spec is the contract: a compliant recipient (or a future Order revision that switches to header-based dedup as the spec text mandates) will 400 every checkout request with `VALIDATION_ERROR: Idempotency-Key != orderId`. Cancel-on-checkout-failure, reservation.create, and payment.intent.create receivers similarly check the header per spec — code only happens to work today because inventory and order accept body fields. This is exactly the type of contract drift that turns into a P0 the day a recipient is fixed to follow the spec.
findings.recommendation: Add a `idempotencyKeyOption(orderID string)` helper alongside bearerAuthOption / internalSecretOption that sets `Idempotency-Key: <orderID>` on the outgoing request. Apply it to: client_inventory.CreateReservation, client_inventory.ReleaseReservation, client_order.CreateFromCheckout, client_order.CancelOnCheckoutFailure, client_payment.CreateIntent. Drop the redundant `idempotencyKey` field from the body where the spec only declares the header (verify per-recipient before removing). Add a unit test that the outgoing request carries Idempotency-Key matching orderID.

findings.topic: Compensation calls run on raw context.Background() with no overall deadline. Per-attempt timeouts are 1s and the loop has 4 attempts (initial + 3 retries) with 50/200/800ms backoff, so a single compensation can run ~5s. With BOTH compensations sequential in step 8 (cancel + release), worst-case is ~10s — held inside the open checkout tx, with the idempotency_keys row locked and INFLIGHT.
findings.locus: backend/services/checkout/app/checkout/handler_commit.go:417 (ReleaseReservation context.Background() at step 7 compensation), :446 (CancelOnCheckoutFailure context.Background() at step 8a), :455 (ReleaseReservation context.Background() at step 8b); client_inventory.go:161-204 (no outer-loop deadline); client_order.go:120-164 (same)
findings.description: Using context.Background() instead of c.Request.Context() is correct in spirit — we don't want a client cancel to abort cleanup. But there is no upper bound on the total compensation duration. The idempotency_keys row is locked through the wrapping pgx tx (handler_commit.go:84) for the entire compensation; concurrent retries with the same Idempotency-Key see 409 INFLIGHT (good), but if the recipient is genuinely down, all 4 attempts × 1s = 4s + cumulative backoff = ~5.05s of held lock per branch, ~10.1s for the step-8 cancel-then-release pair. PERF-002 (p95 500ms) covers the success path only, but the failure path now grossly exceeds the 5s global request budget declared in td.json §timeouts_and_retries_summary. Server-side write timeout is 10s (main.go:31) so the worst case is right at the wire.
findings.recommendation: Wrap each compensation invocation in `ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 6*time.Second); defer cancel()` and pass the bounded ctx into ReleaseReservation / CancelOnCheckoutFailure. The compensation client already obeys ctx.Done in its inter-attempt sleep (client_inventory.go:170, client_order.go:129), so a deadline cuts retries cleanly. Alternative: add an outer compensation budget inside the client itself by computing `deadlineCtx, _ := context.WithTimeout(ctx, totalBudget)` at function entry and using it for both the per-attempt timeout and the sleep selector. Either way, document the cap in td.json §timeouts_and_retries_summary. Recommended cap: 5s per compensation step (matches global budget).

findings.topic: Catalog fan-out (step 4a) treats ALL non-nil errors from catalog.product.detail as PRODUCT_INACTIVE, including transient 5xx / connection failures. The misclassification is then cached for 24h in idempotency_keys, freezing the user out of re-attempting with the same key.
findings.description: Step 4a's per-line classifier: `if detailErrors[i] != nil || d.ProductID == "" { catalogBlockers = append(... PRODUCT_INACTIVE) }` — a 504 timeout, a 503, or a connection-refused all collapse to 'PRODUCT_INACTIVE'. The handler then finalizes the idempotency row with `catalogBlockers` and returns 409 PRODUCT_INACTIVE. On retry with the same key, the cached envelope is replayed verbatim (handler_commit.go:127-136) — even if catalog has since recovered. The customer sees 'product is inactive' for 24h until the idempotency TTL elapses or they generate a new key. handler_preview.go:138-145 has the same bug. Spec td.json §step 3 failure_propagation says only 'NOT_FOUND → mark non-checkoutable'.
findings.recommendation: Distinguish UpstreamError code from generic errors. If errors.As(err, &UpstreamError{Code:NOT_FOUND}) → blocker PRODUCT_INACTIVE / PRODUCT_DELETED based on response status field. Else → set a separate `var fanoutFailed bool` and short-circuit to 504 UPSTREAM_TIMEOUT for the WHOLE commit (do not finalize the idempotency row with COMPLETED + cached error envelope; finalize as ABANDONED so retries can re-enter). Same fix in handler_preview.go.

findings.topic: IdempotencyStatus is declared in two places: app/checkout/domain.go:13-19 and app/checkout/access/storage_idempotency.go:17-23 — same constants, same string values. Risk: future drift if one side is updated (e.g. a new state) and the other is not.
findings.description: Both files define `type IdempotencyStatus string` and the trio (`StatusInflight`, `StatusCompleted`, `StatusAbandoned`). The handler uses access.StatusCompleted (etc) consistently; the domain.go copy is currently unreferenced by the handler. Dead code + a name-collision trap.
findings.recommendation: Delete the domain.go copy. If a domain-layer alias is desired, declare `type IdempotencyStatus = access.IdempotencyStatus` and re-export the constants with `var (StatusInflight = access.StatusInflight; ...)`.

findings.topic: computeRequestHash relies on Go's stable map-key sort in json.Marshal (since Go 1.12) but does NOT canonicalize whitespace inside json.RawMessage values. For the current flat schema {shippingAddressId} this is moot; for any future nested field it will produce different hashes for semantically-identical bodies, causing spurious 409 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED on legitimate retries.
findings.description: Two clients submitting `{"shippingAddressId":"a","foo":{"x":1,"y":2}}` and `{"shippingAddressId":"a","foo":{"y":2,"x":1}}` produce different hashes today. Acknowledged in code comments. The TD §request_hash_algorithm calls for sha256(canonicalize(body)) with sorted keys + normalized whitespace + lowercased hex — only the first part is implemented.
findings.recommendation: Adopt a canonical-JSON library (gibson042/canonicaljson-go or rsc.io/cmp) before any field beyond shippingAddressId is added to the commit body. Track as tech-debt; not blocking for MVP.

findings.topic: extractBearer uses strings.TrimPrefix which silently returns the unchanged string if the 'Bearer ' prefix is absent — so a malformed Authorization header would be forwarded as-is to downstream services. The JWT middleware already rejects requests without the prefix, so this is defense-in-depth only.
findings.description: If a future change moves JWT validation to a place where the prefix isn't pre-checked, extractBearer would forward whatever is in the header — possibly leaking unintended tokens. Today the JWT middleware (router.go:43) validates before the handler runs, so the issue is theoretical.

findings.topic: The variable `committed` in Service.Commit (handler_commit.go:89) is set to true on rollback paths to suppress the deferred rollback. The name implies 'tx was committed' but it really means 'tx is finalized (committed OR rolled back)'. Cosmetic.
findings.description: Reading the code top-down, the eye trips on `committed = true` immediately after `_ = tx.Rollback(...)`. Naming for intent.
findings.recommendation: Rename to `txFinalized` or invert the guard with an explicit `txState` enum. Optional.

hot_zone_compliance.idempotency_key_per_customer_scope: PASS — migrations/001_create_idempotency_keys.up.sql:17 PRIMARY KEY (key, customer_user_id); handler uses claims.Sub (handler_commit.go:75); body never sources customerUserId. CWE-639 clean.
hot_zone_compliance.inflight_race_fix: PASS — TryClaimOrLookup at access/storage_idempotency.go:61-111 uses single-statement `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT (key, customer_user_id) DO NOTHING RETURNING key`. Confirmed correct: the unique-index lock is acquired before any concurrent INSERT proceeds; exactly one caller observes RETURNING with a row. The post-conflict SELECT FOR UPDATE then blocks on the leader's open tx until the row reaches a final state. Closes dry-run #1 H02 race window. Unit test asserts handler-decision matrix at access/storage_idempotency_race_test.go.
hot_zone_compliance.compensation_correctness: MOSTLY PASS — step 6 fail → no compensation (correct, handler_commit.go:373-381). Step 7 fail → ReleaseReservation 3 retries [50,200,800]ms (handler_commit.go:417 + client_inventory.go:165-167). Step 8 fail → CancelOnCheckoutFailure (handler_commit.go:446) THEN ReleaseReservation (handler_commit.go:455), each 3 retries with the spec backoff. Both order client and inventory client use the exact `[50ms, 200ms, 800ms]` slice. CRITICAL log + saga DEGRADED on retry-exhaustion. Note: REV-CHECKOUT-004 raises the unbounded compensation budget concern. The spec wording 'A THEN B' for step 8 is implemented as 'A then B unconditionally' rather than 'A THEN-IF-A-OK B' — both interpretations are defensible; matches the TD's compensation_outcome={notes:[...]} on either-or-both failure.
hot_zone_compliance.server_side_pricing_strict: PASS — handler_helpers.go:45-69 forbiddenFields covers all 9 client-priced names. handler_commit.go:63 calls rejectForbiddenFields BEFORE any orchestration. Step 5 (handler_commit.go:336-360) computes from catalog snapshots, never from the request body. CHK-005 satisfied with defense-in-depth.
hot_zone_compliance.section_11_2_single_source: PASS — pricing.go is the only file containing the 60_00 / 1500_00 literals (verified via grep across backend/services/checkout). ComputeShippingFee is the sole entry point. Boundary inclusive at 1500 THB → 0 (`subtotalMinor < ShippingFeeThreshold` for the fee branch; `>=` falls through to 0). BA-PR-002 honored.
hot_zone_compliance.internal_shared_secret_handling: FAIL — see REV-CHECKOUT-002. INTERNAL_SHARED_SECRET is loaded from env at config.go:71 and threaded into OrderClient (deps.go:53-58); never threaded into InventoryClient or PaymentClient. No secret leakage in logs (grep clean across handler/clients/main). Audit-log of `internal_auth_configured` at startup is not implemented in checkout — but checkout is the CALLER, not a recipient, so the ADR-008 audit-log requirement does not apply here.
hot_zone_compliance.buyer_email_wire: PASS — handler_commit.go:227-232 calls identity.ReadProfile in step 2 and stores `profile.Email`; handler_commit.go:403 threads it into orderCreateRequest.BuyerEmail. ReadProfile timeout 500ms with 1 retry (client_identity.go:53-87). REV-L2-001 closure is correctly implemented. Note: identity.profile.read is currently stubbed (501) per REV-L2-004 — out of scope for this L1 review since the handler error path is wired correctly.
hot_zone_compliance.compensation_context_timeout: PARTIAL — context.Background() is used (correct: client cancellation should not abort cleanup) but no overall deadline is wrapped. See REV-CHECKOUT-004.

passes_observed: Customer JWT role check (CUSTOMER) at handler_helpers.go:96-119; AUTH_FORBIDDEN for ADMIN — covered by handler_commit_test.go.
Idempotency-Key header validation (handler_commit.go:51-55, 531-548) matches spec regex ^[A-Za-z0-9._:-]{1,128}$.
claims.Sub authoritative for customerUserId — never read from body (handler_commit.go:75).
Address ownership via identity.address.list response only (handler_commit.go:236-247) — no direct address-id lookup vulnerable to IDOR.

orderId UUID v7 generated server-side BEFORE step 6 (handler_commit.go:336) — reused as idempotency key for inventory.reservation.create body and order.create-from-checkout body (per the recipient's body-field handler today; HTTP-header gap noted as REV-CHECKOUT-003).
Single tx wraps idempotency_keys + saga_log + downstream HTTP (handler_commit.go:84-94 BeginTx + deferred rollback). Compensation calls correctly run on context.Background() to survive client cancel.
Janitors implemented per spec (main.go:96-141 → access/storage_idempotency.go:180-212). 24h TTL cleanup batch 500 every 5min; stale-INFLIGHT sweep batch 100 every 60s with FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED.
Coupon explicit reject with the spec message at handler_helpers.go:62-65 — CHK-AMBIG-002 chosen path implemented.
Migrations 001 + 002 match td.json §persistence: composite PK, partial indexes, CHECK constraints on status enums.

calibration_check.rationale: Customer-facing buy flow with state spread across 5 services. The two HIGH findings are not theoretical: REV-CHECKOUT-001 makes every successful commit silently roll back the idempotency row (provable from migration column type + handler closure), and REV-CHECKOUT-002 makes every commit fail at step 6 against the actual inventory router (verified the recipient enforces InternalAuthMiddleware). Both pass QA-L1's wire-shape conformance because QA-L1 does not exercise a real DB or real downstream services.
calibration_check.single_family_deviation_defense: Re-derived each handler's flow from td.json §orchestration_pseudocode and connectivity.md before reading the code. Spec demands X-Internal-Secret on inv.reservation.* and payment.intent.create; code only sends it on order.*. Spec demands order_id be NOT NULL only for orchestrations that minted one; code passes empty string unconditionally. These are gaps the code was the wrong source of truth for.
did_not_over_fire_on: Order route mismatch (/api/v1/order/order/create-from-checkout vs spec /api/v1/order/internal/create-from-checkout) — checkout's call matches the order service's actual mount (verified in order/router/router.go:46-54). Cross-component drift; defer to Reviewer-L2.

inventory.stock.bulk-read using Bearer JWT instead of X-Internal-Secret — inventory's actual implementation requires JWT (inventory/router/router.go:65-72). Spec/code drift on the inventory side; defer to Reviewer-L2.

Order client passing both Bearer AND X-Internal-Secret on internal calls — recipient checks only X-Internal-Secret per ADR-008; the extra Bearer is harmless (and avoids needing to remove it before the route alignment lands). Style nit at most.
computeRequestHash using map[string]json.RawMessage — Go's json.Marshal sorts map keys stably; the only gap is whitespace inside RawMessage, captured as REV-CHECKOUT-007 low.
504 vs 503 selection nuances — consistent with sibling services and the cross-cutting error registry.

must_fix_before_merge: REV-CHECKOUT-001 — saga_log empty-UUID aborts wrapping tx; idempotency_keys never finalizes. Affects success path, not just error paths. Without this fix every commit silently rolls back its idempotency state.
REV-CHECKOUT-002 — X-Internal-Secret missing on 3 outbound calls. Recipients enforce InternalAuth → 401 on every commit at step 6, plus customer JWT leak across trust boundaries.
should_fix_post_merge: REV-CHECKOUT-003 — Idempotency-Key header on outbound internal calls (today benign because recipients dedupe on body field; lands as P0 the day a recipient is fixed to the spec).
REV-CHECKOUT-005 — distinguish UpstreamError code from blocker classification (don't pin transient errors as PRODUCT_INACTIVE for 24h).
REV-CHECKOUT-006 — collapse the duplicated IdempotencyStatus type.
